QUESTION PRESENTED
Pursuant to 28 U.S.C. S1651(a) and U.S.Sup.Ct.R. 22, Applicants Joseph Rued,
also o/b/o W.O.R., a minor child, Scott Rued, and Leah Rued respectfully request the
issuance of an emergency injunction to inhibit Defendants below and Respondents
here from sustaining reliance upon the admitted fraud and perjury of Hennepin
County Child Protection Services ("CPS") investigator Respondent Jaykumar
Jayswal's Child in Need of Protection or Services Petition ("CHIPSP"), which has
been admitted to be falsified under oath, and the fraud in conspiracy of other
Defendants relying upon the same, to deprive Constitutionally protected rights of
Applicants pending final adjudication of Applicants'/Petitioners' Petition for Writ of
Certiorari and/or Petition for Writ of Prohibition and, alternatively, Rule Nisi in this
Court.

JURISDICTION
This Emergency Application for Writ of Injunction Pending Adjudication of
Petitions for Writ of Certiorari, Writ of Prohibition, and/or Rule Nisi to this Court is
sought in support of this Court's appellate jurisdiction under 28 U.S.C. 51254(1). The
Jurisdiction of this Court is invoked under 28 U.S.C. S1651(a) and pursuant to
Supreme Court Rule 22. Applicants have made notifications required under 29.4(b).
28 U.S.C. S2403(a) may apply—while Applicants filed necessary notifications under
FRCP 5.1(a)(1) and FRAP 44 to initiate certification to the Attorney General,
Applicants do not have reason to believe such occurred in the lower courts.
STATEMENT OF THE CASE
The district court dismissed Plaintiffs' Complaints in three cases below,
including Plaintiffs' request for emergency injunction, and denied Plaintiffs' motion
to show cause for why an emergency injunction should not issue, fundamentally and
essentially based upon the district court's own fabrications regarding Plaintiffs'
Complaint in 24-CV-1763 (JRT/TNL) (App.-25-26-) and denied Habeas Petitioners
Joseph Rued's ("Rued") and W.O.R.'s Petition for Habeas Corpus fundamentally and
essentially upon the district court's own fabrications regarding Habeas Petitioners'
Petition for Habeas Corpus. The Eighth Circuit summarily affirmed all of the district
2

court's demonstrable fraud upon the court and violations of plain Fifth Amendment
requirements. The frauds and fraud upon the court of the district court are extremely
straightforward to demonstrate and the Eighth Circuit's affirmance of such result in
action the Eighth Circuit plainly has no discretion, authority, or even jurisdiction to
undertake given affirmances of district court determinations that have no possible
basis in the record beyond the district court's own fabrications demonstrable on the
face of the records cannot be construed to be based upon any genuine controversy.
The district court claimed Plaintiffs' Complaint in 24-CV-1763 asserted Rued
"argued" Defendant Jayswal's perjury admissions to Defendant Furnstahl in order to
provide a nexus between Plaintiffs' claims in 24-CV-1763, 24-CV-2437, and 24-CV-
3409 and completed state court proceedings, knowing no completed state court
proceeding had even mentioned, much less considered and determined Jayswal's
admissions of perjury in his CHIPSP allegations against Rued (App.-25-26-) in order
to apply Rooker-Feldman doctrine as a jurisdictional bar in all non-habeas cases.
Similarly, the district court claimed Habeas Petitioners' Petition for Habeas Corpus
sought only relief from child-custody determinations and not physical confinement
unshared by the general public in order to apply caselaw of this Court that relief
under habeas corpus does not lie for challenges to child-custody placements as
children being in custody is shared by the general public, while knowing that Habeas
Petitioners' Petition sought relief from only physical confinement, not child-custody
determinations, imposed in violation of the laws of the United States (App.-188-204-
). The Eighth Circuit affirmed these unlawful actions of the district court (App.-1-6-)
3

knowing such were purely fabricated by the district court and were not based upon
any genuine case or controversy (App.-112-135-).
The unlawful and illegal actions for which Plaintiffs/Appellants below and
Applicants here seek emergency injunction are also extremely straightforward to
demonstrate as unlawful and illegally utilized in violation of Fourteenth Amendment
